Chapter 4: Deliberate Focus and the Art of Allowing
Once you start to really see how your thoughts, feelings, and beliefs play off each other, the next step is all about getting intentional with your focus.
Deliberate focus is simply choosing where you want your attention to go, instead of letting it wander to whatever’s most familiar or urgent. Ever notice how easy it is to get caught up in worries or distractions? What if you could gently guide your mind somewhere that actually serves you?
Now, this isn’t about ignoring real problems or pretending your challenges don’t exist. Here’s something important: your attention is a creative powerhouse. When you focus on what you want—rather than what you fear or resent—you start channeling energy toward new solutions and possibilities.
This brings us to the art of allowing. Allowing is trusting your desires to unfold, without constantly stepping in with doubt or worry. Think of it like planting a seed: you give it the right conditions, but you don’t dig it up every day to make sure it’s growing. You let it be. You trust the process.
You can practice deliberate focus in everyday moments. Say you’re facing a challenge—try asking yourself, “What’s one thing I actually appreciate about this situation?” Or, “What outcome would I love to see here?” These kinds of questions gently shift your attention from the problem to what’s possible, and suddenly, new solutions can begin to show up.
Allowing also means letting go of the urge to control every single detail. It’s not about giving up on your desires—it’s about trusting that the process is unfolding, even if you can’t see exactly how it’s all going to work out. Patience and trust really are key here.
So, how can you start weaving deliberate focus and allowing into your daily life?
Try setting aside just a few minutes each day to picture your desired outcomes—really focus on how those outcomes would feel.
When doubts pop up—and they will—just notice them without judgment. Then, gently bring your attention back to what you want.
And don’t forget about gratitude. Taking time to appreciate what you already have shifts your focus toward abundance, not lack.
Small shifts in focus and a little more allowing can make a big difference. It’s about guiding your energy, one moment at a time, toward the life you want to create.
